# Notification Channels & Subscriptions

You manage Facets notifications via `raptor` commands in Bash.

There are two entities, and they are **Control Plane-global** — not scoped to a blueprint
branch, PR, or environment:

- A **channel** is a delivery destination (a Slack webhook, an email list, a PagerDuty
  service, …). It has a `channelType` and type-specific fields.
- A **subscription** routes one **notification type** (e.g. `ALERT`, `APP_DEPLOYMENT`) to a
  channel, narrowed by **filters**. Which filters are valid depends on the notification type.

The two hard things this skill exists to get right:

1. **Channel fields are conditional on `channelType`** — a Slack channel needs a webhook URL,
   an email channel needs addresses, a PagerDuty channel needs an integration key.
2. **Subscription filters are conditional on the notification type** — and the matrix is
   **backend-driven**, so it can change. Two filters (environment vs release stream) are
   mutually exclusive.

## THE GOLDEN RULE — discover, don't guess

The type→tag matrix and the valid values for each tag are served by the Control Plane and
**can change between versions**. The tables in this skill are a verified snapshot for quick
reference, but when you are about to build a real subscription, confirm against the live API:

```bash
raptor get notification-types                              # every type + the filter tags each supports
raptor get notification-tags --type APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE   # the exact keys/labels a type accepts
raptor get notification-tag-values --type APP_DEPLOYMENT --tag CLUSTER_NAME -p PROJECT   # valid values for a tag
raptor get notification-attributes --type APP_DEPLOYMENT   # webhook payload {{fields}} a type exposes
```

`get notification-tag-values` **cascades**: `STACK_NAME` (`-p`) narrows `CLUSTER_NAME`, which
narrows `APPLICATION_NAME`. Pass the upstream context to get a relevant list:

```bash
raptor get notification-tag-values --type APP_DEPLOYMENT --tag APPLICATION_NAME -p PROJECT --environment prod-env
```

## Conventions

- **id or name:** every single-entity command (`get`/`set`/`delete`/`test`) accepts the
  entity's **ID or its unique name** — names are unique-indexed server-side, so use whichever
  is handier.
- **Aliases:** `channels`=`channel`; `subscriptions`=`subscription`=`subs`=`sub`.
- **Output:** `-o table` (default), `-o wide`, `-o json`, `-o yaml`. Use `-o json` to read
  the full `filters` map back.
- **Input model:** convenience flags for common cases, or `-f FILE` (JSON **or** YAML) for a
  full payload. `set` is **read-modify-write** (only the flags you pass change); `-f` on `set`
  is a **full replace**.
- **No `-p`/`-e` on channels.** Channels are global. `-p` appears only on subscriptions (it is
  the `STACK_NAME` filter — see below).
- **Debugging:** `RAPTOR_DEBUG=1 raptor …` prints every request URL, headers, and response
  body — including the values-API calls and any enum-error 500s during a create.

## Channels

### Channel types and their conditional fields

raptor passes whatever fields you set straight through; it does **not** enforce per-type
required fields client-side (the Control Plane does). Supply the fields that match the type:

| `channelType`        | Required field(s)                     | Flag(s)                          | Notes |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------|-------|
| `SLACK`              | webhook URL                           | `--address`                      | `https://hooks.slack.com/services/…` |
| `WEBHOOK`            | endpoint URL                          | `--address` [`--auth-header`]    | `--auth-header` sets an `Authorization` header (optional) |
| `EMAIL`              | recipient emails                      | `--emails a@x,b@y`               | comma-separated |
| `PAGER_DUTY`         | routing/integration key               | `--integration-key` [`--address`]| `--address` is the Events API URL (`https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue`) |
| `ZEN_DUTY`           | events URL (key embedded)             | `--address` [`--integration-key`]| `https://www.zenduty.com/api/events/UUID/` |
| `MS_TEAMS`           | incoming-webhook URL                  | `--address`                      | classic Teams connector URL |
| `MS_TEAMS_WORKFLOW`  | Power Automate workflow URL           | `--address`                      | the Workflows (not connector) URL |

> **`CAPILLARY_VALIDATOR` is internal.** It exists in the backend enum but is **not** a
> user-facing channel type — never offer it. The seven types above are the public set.

### Channel commands

```bash
# Create (type-driven fields)
raptor create channel oncall --type SLACK --address https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX
raptor create channel team   --type EMAIL --emails a@example.com,b@example.com
raptor create channel pd      --type PAGER_DUTY --integration-key 0123456789abcdef --address https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue
raptor create channel hook    --type WEBHOOK --address https://example.com/hook --auth-header "Bearer xyz"
raptor create channel -f channel.yaml                      # full payload (any type)

# List / show (by id or name)
raptor get channels
raptor get channels oncall -o yaml
raptor get channels -o wide                                # ID, NAME, TYPE, ADDRESS, EMAILS, INTEGRATION-KEY

# Update (read-modify-write — only the flags you pass change)
raptor set channel oncall --address https://hooks.slack.com/services/NEW
raptor set channel hook --auth-header "Bearer rotated"

# Delete (one or more, by id or name; -y skips the confirm prompt)
raptor delete channel oncall stale-webhook -y

# Test — send a real test notification (see "Testing" below)
raptor test channel oncall
```

## Subscriptions

A subscription = **notification type** + **channel** + **filters** (+ optional subject).

### The rules that bite

1. **`-p/--project` is required for every type EXCEPT `AUDIT_LOG`.** It becomes the mandatory
   `STACK_NAME` filter and the subscription's top-level `stackName`. `AUDIT_LOG` may be global
   (no `-p`). Omitting `-p` on a non-audit type is a clear pre-flight error.
2. **Environment ⊕ release stream.** `--environment` (`CLUSTER_NAME`) and `--release-stream`
   (`CLUSTER_TYPE`) are **mutually exclusive** — a subscription scopes by specific environments
   **or** by release stream, never both. Passing both is rejected before any API call. The
   guard runs on the assembled filter map, so it also catches both keys arriving via
   `--filter`, a mix, a `set` merge, or a `-f` file.
   - **Locked on edit:** because `set` is read-modify-write, you cannot switch from environment
     to release stream by just passing the other flag (the existing one is preserved → both
     present → rejected). This is intentional parity with the UI (which disables the toggle on
     edit). To switch, use `-f` (full replace) or delete + recreate.
3. **Filter values are names, not IDs** — environment name, app name, release-stream name. The
   exception: `AUDIT_ENTITY`/`AUDIT_ACTION` take the **enum** name (`BLUEPRINT`,
   `BLUEPRINT_CREATE`), not the display text ("Blueprint").
4. **The channel** is given by `--channel ID` or `--channel-name NAME` (resolved to its id).

### Subscription commands

```bash
# Create
raptor create subscription deploys -p infra-dev --type APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE \
  --channel-name oncall --application api --environment prod-env \
  --filter DEPLOYMENT_STATUS=SUCCEEDED,FAILED

raptor create subscription -f subscription.yaml            # full payload

# List / show (by id or name)
raptor get subscriptions
raptor get subscriptions deploys -o yaml

# Update (read-modify-write; each filter flag replaces only that one key)
raptor set subscription deploys --channel-name pagerduty-oncall
raptor set subscription deploys --filter DEPLOYMENT_STATUS=FAILED

# Delete (one or more; -y skips confirm)
raptor delete subscription deploys old-sub -y

# Test
raptor test subscription deploys
```

### Filters: how to pass them

The three near-universal tags have convenience flags; everything else uses the generic
`--filter`:

| Convenience flag      | Tag key            | Notes |
|-----------------------|--------------------|-------|
| `-p` / `--project`    | `STACK_NAME`       | required (except `AUDIT_LOG`) |
| `--environment`       | `CLUSTER_NAME`     | env names; **excl.** with `--release-stream` |
| `--release-stream`    | `CLUSTER_TYPE`     | release-stream names; **excl.** with `--environment` |
| `--application`       | `APPLICATION_NAME` | app names |
| `--filter KEY=value`  | any other tag      | repeatable; `;` joins pairs; `,` joins values |

`--filter` accepts the whole set in one quoted flag, `;`-separated; `,` gives a key multiple
values. Whitespace is **not** a separator (a value may contain spaces). These are equivalent:

```bash
--filter SEVERITY=critical,warning --filter ALERT_NAME=HighCPU --filter SEND_RESOLVED=false
--filter "SEVERITY=critical,warning;ALERT_NAME=HighCPU;SEND_RESOLVED=false"
```

## Filter matrix — which tags go with which notification type

Snapshot from `raptor get notification-types` (the **authoritative** list — re-run it to
confirm). `STACK_NAME` (`-p`) applies to all of these except `AUDIT_LOG` and is omitted from
the columns. "Environment scope" = `CLUSTER_NAME` (`--environment`) **or** `CLUSTER_TYPE`
(`--release-stream`), never both.

| Notification type                  | Environment scope | Other valid filter tags |
|------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|
| `APP_DEPLOYMENT`                   | env / release     | `APPLICATION_NAME` |
| `APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE`  | env / release     | `APPLICATION_NAME`, `DEPLOYMENT_STATUS` |
| `DEPLOYMENT_STATUS_UPDATE`         | env / release     | `DEPLOYMENT_STATUS`, `RELEASE_TYPE` |
| `ALERT`                            | env / release     | `SEVERITY`, `ALERT_NAME`, `SEND_RESOLVED` |
| `SHORT_LIVED_ENVIRONMENT_TEARDOWN` | env (`CLUSTER_NAME`) | `ENVIRONMENT_TEARDOWN_NOTIFY_BEFORE` (numeric) |
| `ENVIRONMENT_CREATE`               | — (none)          | — |
| `ENVIRONMENT_DELETE`               | env (`CLUSTER_NAME`) | — |
| `ENVIRONMENT_LAUNCH`               | env (`CLUSTER_NAME`) | — |
| `ENVIRONMENT_DESTROY`              | env (`CLUSTER_NAME`) | — |
| `ENVIRONMENT_CONFIGURE`            | env (`CLUSTER_NAME`) | — |
| `STACK_SIGNOFF`                    | — (none)          | — |
| `AUDIT_LOG`                        | `CLUSTER_NAME`    | `AUDIT_ENTITY`, `AUDIT_ACTION` — **global; `-p` optional** |

**Extended types** — `DR_RESULT` and `QASUITE_SANITY` are accepted at create but are **not
returned by `get notification-types`**, so `get notification-tags`/`-tag-values` won't help for
them. Pass their filters via raw `--filter`:

| Notification type | Environment scope | Other tags (raw `--filter`) |
|-------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| `DR_RESULT`       | env / release     | `DR_ACTION`, `DR_STATUS` (`DR_STATUS` has no value provider) |
| `QASUITE_SANITY`  | env / release     | `QASUITE_RESULT` |

### Tag → flag and values reference

| Tag                                  | How to pass                         | Valid values |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------|
| `STACK_NAME`                         | `-p PROJECT`                        | a project name |
| `CLUSTER_NAME`                       | `--environment` / `--filter`        | environment names (e.g. `prod-env`) |
| `CLUSTER_TYPE`                       | `--release-stream` / `--filter`     | release-stream names (e.g. `PROD`, `STAGING`, `TEST`) |
| `APPLICATION_NAME`                   | `--application` / `--filter`        | application/service names |
| `DEPLOYMENT_STATUS`                  | `--filter`                          | `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` |
| `RELEASE_TYPE`                       | `--filter`                          | discover (`get notification-tag-values`) |
| `SEVERITY`                           | `--filter`                          | `critical`, `warning` |
| `ALERT_NAME`                         | `--filter`                          | free text (alert name) |
| `SEND_RESOLVED`                      | `--filter`                          | `true`, `false` |
| `ENVIRONMENT_TEARDOWN_NOTIFY_BEFORE` | `--filter`                          | a number of minutes (e.g. `30`) |
| `AUDIT_ENTITY`                       | `--filter`                          | **enum** name (e.g. `BLUEPRINT`) — not "Blueprint" |
| `AUDIT_ACTION`                       | `--filter`                          | **enum** name (e.g. `BLUEPRINT_CREATE`) |
| `DR_ACTION` / `DR_STATUS`            | `--filter`                          | discover; `DR_STATUS` is unenumerable (allowed unvalidated) |
| `QASUITE_RESULT`                     | `--filter`                          | discover |

> When unsure of a value, **run `get notification-tag-values`** rather than guessing — it
> returns the exact accepted values (and for audit tags, the enum name to use).

## Recipe — build a correct subscription

1. **Pick the notification type.** Unsure what's available? `raptor get notification-types`.
2. **Find the type's valid filter tags** (matrix above, or `get notification-tags --type T`).
   Passing a tag the type doesn't accept is wrong — stick to its row.
3. **Project:** add `-p PROJECT` (sets `STACK_NAME`). Skip only for `AUDIT_LOG`.
4. **Channel:** `--channel-name NAME` (or `--channel ID`). It must already exist — create it
   first if needed.
5. **Environment scope:** choose `--environment` **XOR** `--release-stream` — never both.
6. **Other tags:** pass via `--filter KEY=value` (combine with `;`). Use **names**, not IDs;
   for audit tags use the **enum** name.
7. **Confirm values** you're unsure about with
   `raptor get notification-tag-values --type T --tag K -p PROJECT [--environment …]`.
8. **Create.** raptor validates the values before creating (see tiers below) and auto-fills
   `channelType`/`channelAddress`/`stackName` so the subscription renders correctly in the UI.

### Worked examples (one per shape)

```bash
# Alert routing — environment-scoped, several filters in one flag
raptor create subscription prod-alerts -p infra-dev --type ALERT --channel-name oncall \
  --environment prod-env \
  --filter "SEVERITY=critical,warning;ALERT_NAME=HighCPU;SEND_RESOLVED=false"

# App deployment complete — release-stream-scoped (NOT environment), success+fail
raptor create subscription deploys -p infra-dev --type APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE \
  --channel-name oncall --release-stream PROD --application api \
  --filter DEPLOYMENT_STATUS=SUCCEEDED,FAILED

# Short-lived env teardown warning — numeric tag, env-scoped
raptor create subscription teardown -p infra-dev --type SHORT_LIVED_ENVIRONMENT_TEARDOWN \
  --channel-name oncall --environment staging --filter ENVIRONMENT_TEARDOWN_NOTIFY_BEFORE=30

# Audit log — GLOBAL (no -p), enum-name filters
raptor create subscription audit --type AUDIT_LOG --channel-name oncall \
  --filter "AUDIT_ENTITY=BLUEPRINT;AUDIT_ACTION=BLUEPRINT_CREATE"

# Environment lifecycle — no extra tags beyond environment
raptor create subscription env-deletes -p infra-dev --type ENVIRONMENT_DELETE \
  --channel-name oncall --environment prod-env
```

## Validation & failure modes

Before a create/update, raptor checks your filter values against the live value lists. Three
tiers — designed so a typo is caught but a legitimate-but-unlistable filter is never blocked:

| Tier      | Trigger | Behavior |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| **ABORT** | values lookup returns a real error, e.g. `No enum constant AuditEntity.Blueprint` | stop, create nothing — the input is bad (fix it, e.g. use `BLUEPRINT`) |
| **ALLOW** | lookup returns `no suitable tag data provider found` (e.g. `DR_STATUS`) | proceed — the tag is a valid filter that just can't be enumerated |
| **WARN**  | lookup succeeds but a value isn't in the set | non-blocking stderr warning (matching is case-insensitive; the set may omit new values) |

### Downstream delivery failures (during `test`)

A `test` can pass at raptor and the Control Plane, then be rejected by the destination — the
error you see is the destination's, wrapped in a 500:

- **Slack `invalid_payload`** — a Slack webhook needs `{"text":"…"}`. A bare `test channel` on
  a WEBHOOK sends `{}`; pass `--payload-json '{"text":"hi"}'`, or use a `SLACK`-typed channel
  (which builds the message for you).
- **Slack `invalid_token` / Teams `403`** — the webhook URL is wrong, truncated, or revoked.
- **`UnknownHostException` / connection errors** — the destination host is unreachable from the
  Control Plane; the raptor/CP path still worked.

## Testing notifications

`test channel` / `test subscription` send a **real** notification through the same notifier the
platform uses, and are rate-limited per user per day. Two modes each:

```bash
# By reference — resolve a saved channel/subscription (id or name)
raptor test channel oncall
raptor test subscription deploys

# Ad-hoc — test a config WITHOUT saving it first
raptor test channel --type WEBHOOK --address https://postman-echo.com/post
raptor test channel --type SLACK --address https://hooks.slack.com/... --payload-json '{"text":"hi"}'
raptor test subscription --channel-name oncall --type ALERT
```

- `--payload-json` is honored for **WEBHOOK** channels only (Slack/Teams/PagerDuty/ZenDuty/
  Email build their own message). For a webhook test with no payload, raptor sends `{}` (the
  notifier compiles the body as a template and NPEs on null).
- **For safe smoke tests, point a throwaway WEBHOOK channel at a request bin** like
  `https://postman-echo.com/post` or `https://webhook.site/…` — `test` delivers to the real
  destination, so don't spam a live Slack/Teams channel.

---

## Webhook payload templating (`--payload-json`)

For a **WEBHOOK** channel you can override the request body with `--payload-json` on the
subscription. On delivery the Control Plane renders it as a **Mustache template** (HTML-escaping
off) against the notification's data. Other channel types (Slack/Teams/PagerDuty/ZenDuty/Email)
ignore `--payload-json` and build their own message.

**Keys vs. fields — they behave differently:**
- The JSON **keys** (property names) are yours to name freely — `{"app":"{{resourceName}}"}` is
  fine. The payload string is **never validated at create/update**; it is stored verbatim.
- The `{{…}}` **values** must be real **attributes** of the type. The renderer is **strict**:
  an unknown placeholder does **not** render empty — it makes delivery fail with
  `500: No method or field with name '…'`. (Caught only at send time, since create/update
  doesn't render.) So name keys however you like, but every `{{placeholder}}` must come from
  `get notification-attributes --type T`. Static values (no placeholder) are always fine.

**Discover the available `{{fields}}` — don't guess.** They are per-type and can change across
Control Plane versions, so list them from the live API before writing a payload:

```bash
raptor get notification-attributes --type APP_DEPLOYMENT
# applicationName  releaseType  artifactUri  hostName  integrationKey  stackName  clusterName  clusterId  notificationMessage
```

Every type also exposes the **base fields** on top of its type-specific ones: `{{stackName}}`,
`{{clusterName}}`, `{{clusterId}}`, `{{notificationMessage}}`, `{{integrationKey}}`,
`{{hostName}}`, `{{encodedHostName}}`. Type-specific examples: `ALERT` adds `alertSeverity`,
`alertStatus`, `alertMessage`, `resourceName`, `resolved`, `pod`, `namespace`, …;
`APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE` adds `resourceName`, `resourceType`, `deploymentStatus`,
`buildId`; `AUDIT_LOG` adds `entity`, `entityAction`, `performedBy`, `performedAt`, `target`.
Boolean fields (e.g. `resolved`) work as Mustache sections: `{{#resolved}}…{{/resolved}}`.

Example — a webhook subscription whose body uses the type's attributes:

```bash
raptor create subscription deploy-hook -p infra-dev --type APPLICATION_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE \
  --channel-name my-webhook --filter DEPLOYMENT_STATUS=SUCCEEDED,FAILED \
  --payload-json '{"text":"{{resourceName}} in {{clusterName}} → {{deploymentStatus}}","build":"{{buildId}}"}'
```

> **`test` uses random values.** `test subscription`/`test channel` fill these attributes with
> randomly-generated data, so a test only proves the template parses and the endpoint is
> reachable — not that real values map correctly.

---

## Caveats cheat-sheet

- **id or name** works everywhere a single entity is referenced.
- **`-p` is the `STACK_NAME` filter** (and sets top-level `stackName`). Required for all types
  but `AUDIT_LOG`.
- **environment ⊕ release-stream** — pick one; locked on edit (switch via `-f` or recreate).
- **filter values are names, not IDs**; audit tags use **enum** names, not display text.
- **`--filter`**: repeat it, or pass several pairs in one quoted flag with `;`; `,` gives a key
  multiple values; whitespace is not a separator.
- **`set` merges** (per-key filter replace); **`-f` replaces** the whole entity.
- **`--payload-json` is WEBHOOK-only** — a Mustache template; list its `{{fields}}` with `get notification-attributes --type T`.
- **empty/whitespace `-f` files are rejected** (so you can't accidentally create an empty entity).
- **`CAPILLARY_VALIDATOR` is internal** — never present it as a channel type.
- **`test` sends real notifications** and is rate-limited.
- **the type→tag matrix is backend-driven** — `get notification-types` / `get
  notification-tags` are the source of truth; the tables here are a snapshot.

## Under the hood

Backed by `UiNotificationController` at `cc-ui/v1/notification/*`. For the full design
(endpoints, DTOs, the type→tag matrix, discovery, exclusivity, and validation tiers) see
`docs/2026-06-23-notification-channel-subscription-design.md` in the raptor repo.
